biggest_catch: The $95 annual fee comes out of the bonus: 75,000 miles (about $750 in travel value at 1 cent per mile through Capital One Travel) minus the $95 fee leaves roughly $655 of first-year net value, and only if you hit $4,000 in 3 months with spending you already planned.
catches: Claim the bonus only with spending you already planned; never buy things you don't need just to hit the $4,000 target.
The $95 annual fee reduces the bonus — first-year net math is in the biggest catch above.
Applying for the card causes a hard credit inquiry, which can temporarily lower your credit score.
The purchase APR is roughly 20%+; carrying a balance for even a month or two wipes out the bonus value — pay the statement balance in full every month.
You are ineligible if you received a new-cardmember bonus for a Venture or Venture X account in the past 48 months (Capital One's family-level 48-month rule).
The bonus posts within two billing cycles, not immediately — keep the account open until it lands.

steps: Go to the official Capital One page https://www.capitalone.com/credit-cards/travel-and-miles/ and read the Venture welcome-bonus terms (75,000 miles after $4,000 in 3 months).
Confirm you have not received a Venture or Venture X new-cardmember bonus in the past 48 months.
Apply online through that official page and get approved; save your approval confirmation.
Within the first 3 months, put $4,000 of already-planned purchases on the card — never extra spending for the bonus.
Pay the statement balance in full every month at ~20%+ APR; do not carry a balance.
Watch for the 75,000 miles to post within two billing cycles of hitting the spend.
If you book hotels/vacation rentals, use the separate one-time $300 Capital One Travel Stays credit in your first cardholder year before it expires.
timing: Bonus miles post within two billing cycles after you meet the $4,000-in-3-months spend requirement.
